medium_findings.scanner_message: Using xml.etree.ElementTree.parse to parse untrusted XML data is known to be vulnerable to XML attacks. Replace xml.etree.ElementTree.parse with its defusedxml equivalent function or make sure defusedxml.defuse_stdlib() is called
medium_findings.disposition: reviewed bounded call site; retained without suppression
medium_findings.assessment: The release runner parses pytest-generated JUnit artifacts under the project artifacts directory, not an HTTP upload or general untrusted XML input. The writer/output path and assertion-enabled execution are controlled by the reviewed runner. Keep those local evidence inputs trusted; ElementTree is not approved here for arbitrary third-party XML.

medium_findings.scanner_message: Audit url open for permitted schemes. Allowing use of file:/ or custom schemes is often unexpected.
medium_findings.disposition: reviewed bounded call site; retained without suppression
medium_findings.assessment: All callers use fixed HTTPS OSV endpoints, with advisory IDs URL-encoded and only public package names/versions submitted. Responses/timeouts/retries are bounded. This local audit helper is not a public/general-purpose URL-fetch API and is not approved for untrusted arbitrary URLs.

low_category_assessments.assessment: Maintenance, benchmark, dbt/Airflow and CI subprocesses use argument arrays without shell=True and explicit owned process handles. Executable paths/PATH and the host remain trusted configuration; arbitrary executable/environment compromise is outside this claim.
Seeded benchmark Random shuffles synthetic workloads; credentials use secrets, not Random.
The captured token_type=bearer protocol label is not an embedded credential.
ElementTree import belongs to the same trusted pytest-JUnit evidence boundary as medium B314; do not reuse this parser for arbitrary untrusted XML.

limitations: Every raw finding is retained. Dispositions apply only to the bound code and are not blanket security or exploitability claims.
The previous static-triage.json remains historical and is not overwritten in the repository.
The production HTTP auth/job boundaries have separate signature/database/runtime tests; static scanners do not prove them.
